correctness.rationale: Necessity and sufficiency prove exactly the interval-plus-tail-prefix classification for all c≥3,t≥1, including the hub initially white and hub initially blue. The rotational interval counts give the entire polynomial. A coefficient difference identity proves unimodality for all parameters, while a strict three-coefficient determinant and exhaustive elementary boundary cases prove the exact log-concavity criterion. The checker constructs the graph directly and independently confirms 34 exhaustive examples (46,608 subsets), then verifies 1,680 parameter-level arithmetic cases; finite checks are corroborative, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The parameter of exactly one pendant vertex defines a natural complete class of connected unicyclic graphs and the 2026 Problem 5.2 asks precisely for unicyclic connected-forcing polynomials. The result computes every size of forcing set and the exact total across all cycle and tail lengths; it also proves a sharp shape dichotomy: universal unimodality despite log-concavity failure exactly when c≥5,t≥2. This distinguishes structurally meaningful graph boundaries and supplies a test family for future broader unicyclic polynomial results, beyond the old scalar minimum.
